subject: Procurement: SLO access & temporary exception guardrails
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightbridge.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement, alerting, and dashboard access

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our procurement packet. A few clarifying questions on SLOs and operational access before we move to legal:

1) SLO definitions: how do you measure uptime/availability for the hosted API? What are the exact signal sources (ingest hops, LB, runtime health) and what measurement window do you use for p95/p99 latency?

2) Sampling & exclusions: do you exclude scheduled maintenance, retries, background system traffic? If so, how is that recorded?

3) Alerting & mean time to respond: what alerts are emitted to customers vs internal on-call? Are there automatic page escalations?

4) Customer visibility: can we get a read-only dashboard with historical 6 months of p95/p99 and per-region uptimes? If you cannot provide 6 months, what is the maximum retention?

5) Temporary exceptions: we are asking for a short-term exception to your standard SLO access policy during our onboarding pilot (30–60 days). What guardrails do you require to approve ephemeral dashboard access?

We know this is a lot — if useful, we can do a quick call. Closing deadline for our procurement committee is 12/15.

Appreciate it,

Lisa Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightBridge Analytics

Attachments: procurement_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (referenced)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.example.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@brightbridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement, alerting, and dashboard access

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching a compact SLO packet for the committee. Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer.

1) Measurement sources: availability is computed from our API gateway's health checks plus per-instance runtime health signals merged with LB success rates. Latency is measured at ingress (request acceptance) and at token-emit for generation calls; p95/p99 are computed over a rolling 30-day window by default. We include per-region aggregations.

2) Sampling & exclusions: Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded and logged in our maintenance calendar (audit trail available). Automated retry traffic that we generate for backfilling is tagged and excluded from customer-facing SLO calculations. Unrecoverable service failures are included; transient infra retries are filtered using a deterministic filter.

3) Alerting: We emit two classes of alerts — customer-facing SLA incidents (email + status page entry) and operational pages (PagerDuty). Customer-facing incidents include a short human-friendly summary; operator pages include playbook links. Mean time to initial response for priority incidents is 30 minutes for Dedicated customers; hosted tier is 1 hour.

4) Customer visibility & retention: For Dedicated and Private customers we provide a read-only Grafana dashboard with 12 months retention by default. For Hosted/API customers we provide 90 days of metrics on the standard dashboard. If you need 6 months for proof-of-concept, we can enable a time-limited 6-month view as a temporary exception.

5) Temporary exceptions & guardrails: We can approve time-limited read-only dashboard access under the following conditions:
  • Access is strictly read-only and IP-restricted to your corporate CIDR(s)
  • Access window limited to 30 days initially; can be extended to 60 days with written justification
  • All access is audited; we will provide an audit log export at the end of the window
  • No direct query-level exports (CSV download) unless agreed in writing

Attachments: SLO_Metrics_Definitions.pdf (summary of signals, windows, and sample queries)

Proposed next step: if that aligns, I can work with infra to provision a read-only invite and route the approval through our procurement exceptions workflow.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
